interpretation: The FFW-vs-ML KPI's headline finding (physical B3 R^2=0.5972 beats ML B4 R^2=0.4536 by +0.1436, claim_lock physics_wins_ml_loses_documented_honestly=true) is a single point-estimate comparison, seed=0, on a test set of 194 rows drawn from only 13 independent polymer chemistries -- fewer clusters than the published rule-of-thumb threshold (G>=~30) below which cluster-robust inference is known to be unreliable (Cameron, Gelbach & Miller 2008; Cameron & Miller 2015). The KPI JSON body contains zero bootstrap, confidence-interval, cluster, jackknife, or standard-error tokens anywhere. Its own sibling KPI -- built on the IDENTICAL 41-train/13-test polymer partition (cross-linked by matching conformal_receipt_sha256) -- DOES apply this level of scrutiny to itself, explicitly documenting that its own R^2=0.4535 is far below the parent's source-safe R^2=0.944, and that marginal conformal coverage hides a conditional-coverage collapse in the worst applicability-domain quintile (194 test rows split into 5 quintiles, ~39 rows/quintile on average; worst-quintile coverage 0.379 vs marginal 0.897). This audit does NOT dispute the FFW-vs-ML numbers themselves -- the positive-control check above confirms they are internally self-consistent (RMSE/R^2 imply an identical SS_tot/n=5.731677 across all 5 baselines, to 1e-6 relative precision). What is refuted is the claim_lock's implicit assertion that the finding is 'documented honestly' to the standard the module itself already applies one file over: a headline result resting on only 13 independent chemical units, with zero quantified uncertainty, is not disclosed as fragile the way the sibling KPI's small-n findings are.
